## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
data.title: Audit merge gate treats commits on other refs (worklog/backup) as dev integration evidence

# Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

## Objective

Make `implement.py finish`'s test gate validate the exact tree the commit
will produce, and make every gate verdict self-describing (which tree ran,
whether it came from cache). A green gate must never again be produced by a
suite run against a different tree or by a stale cached result.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` runs the test gate **before** it stages and commits
(`git_commit` performs `git add -A` afterwards). Suite tests that key off the
**tracked** file set (`git ls-files`) therefore cannot see files the commit is
about to add, and the gate can report a green full-scope run for a tree that
is red the moment the commit lands. The false green is silent: the report says
"full scope, success", so no agent looks further, and the tree stays red at
the push, in CI, and for the next agent.

Observed on ContentCreator work item **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** (Ep 1 of *Inside
the Content Creation Suite*):

- `implement.py finish` reported `{"tooling": "suite", "scope": "full",
  "success": true}` and pushed commit `9c88625c`.
- A full-suite run on the same tree immediately after reported **2 failed**,
  both caused by the newly added files:
  - `test_no_podcast_episode_content_tracked_outside_documented_leftovers` —
    `podcasts/ep1-why-use-it/*` were not yet in `git ls-files`, so the
    allowlist guard passed pre-commit and failed post-commit.
  - `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` — the wiki registry was
    stale for the new synthesis page. This test reads **on-disk** files, not
    `git ls-files`, so untracked-invisibility cannot explain its false pass.
- The item was re-finished (`9f3a1f6c`) after fixing the allowlist and
  rebuilding the metadata; the suite was green at that commit
  (`2765 passed, 16 skipped`). The defect is the false green, not the fix.

Origin record: **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** (ContentCreator worklog) — full intake
brief, investigation trail, and evidence.

## Investigation findings (from the origin intake)

Two mechanisms are supported; both must be closed:

1. **Untracked-file invisibility (proved).** `git_commit` stages *after* the
   test step, and the suite runs against the loose working tree. Anything
   using `git ls-files` semantics cannot see the commit's new files.
2. **Verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree (root
   cause to pin).** Surviving cache evidence: the nearest green full-suite
   entry in the shared `.worklog/cache` (08:53, state `8e9c3ea7…`) collected
   **2751** tests, i.e. the dev tree before the episode work's test files
   existed; the post-commit red run (10:56, `f73d063e…`) collected **2781**,
   matching the committed tree. The gate's own per-worktree cache was deleted
   with the worktree, so the exact entry served cannot be recovered. Because
   the parity test reads disk, untracked-invisibility alone cannot explain its
   pass: the gate either executed against a different checkout/state or served
   a cached result recorded for a different tree.

## Desired change

1. **Temporary-index gate (operator-approved option A).** Before the gate's
   test step: copy the real index to a temp file, apply the change set to the
   copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the suite with
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
   `git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
   index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds; on failure the temp
   index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is currently **not** in `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`
   (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`), so it survives the runner's env scrub —
   this must be asserted by a regression test so a future scrub addition
   cannot silently break the fix.
2. **Verifiable verdicts.** The gate's report must state (a) the tree the
   suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
   result was served from the cache. A cached verdict is acceptable only when
   its fingerprint is the would-be-commit tree's fingerprint; otherwise the
   suite must run.

Rejected: stage-then-test with unstage-on-abort (mutates the real index,
fragile restore); `git status --porcelain`-clean assertion only (demands a
clean tree and still does not test the commit's file set).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file
      rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the
      finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green
      full-scope pass. Reproduced through the finish-gate entry point.
- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran
      against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from
      cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run
      (stale/foreign cache entries must miss).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial
      commit, no residual staging, and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's
      env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's
      cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as
      today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Parity false pass explained:** the regression work reproduces the
      disk-reading parity case at the finish-gate entry point and records the
      root cause (wrong checkout / stale cache / metadata lag before staging)
      in this work item.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass —
      `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
      plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.
- [ ] **Documentation:** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (finish gate
      semantics, verdict provenance), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`
      (cache fingerprint / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` contract) updated. CHANGELOG.md is
      managed by the ship skill and excluded.

## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: no default bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.);
  guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down
  contract stay intact.
- ✗ One suite execution per gate verdict on a clean change set.
- ✗ The changed-scope development gate stays the fast path; the full suite
  stays the dev-push integration gate.
- ✗ Implemented in this repository (framework); do not edit the global install
  directly.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_guarded_suite`, gate report keys.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` / `run_cached` / `cache_dir`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, env construction
  (`subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides`).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py` —
  regression-test homes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** a temporary index changes *staged* status, which may surprise
  tests asserting on working-tree state beyond `git ls-files` (e.g.
  `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in ContentCreator's
  `test_implement_state_gitignore.py`). Mitigation: re-verify such tests in
  the regression work and document the semantics.
- **Risk:** two cache entries per state (loose vs staged fingerprint);
  accepted — correctness over hit ratio.
- **Assumption:** the parity false pass shares the gate-to-tree mismatch
  cause rather than a metadata-lag-only cause; the reproduction settles it.
- **Cross-repo note:** project-level fallout (ContentCreator's missing
  pre-push full-suite gate) is tracked separately in the OSL worklog, not
  here.

## Related work

- **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** — origin record and intake brief (ContentCreator).
- **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** — work item whose first finish produced the false
  green (`9c88625c`, corrected by `9f3a1f6c`).
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — live-repo guard vs pre-push gate duration and
  implement push timeout.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H**, **SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** — guard ownership.
- **OSL-0MUHNOJ8E002YKUO** — accidental `.implement_state.json` tracking via
  the same `git add -A` staging surface.
data.title: Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

Discovered-from: SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ (claim-hold fix).

## Problem
acquireFileLock() (~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts) removes a lock whose acquiredAt is older than DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS (5 min) even when the holder PID is alive on the same host. A long wl sync (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store) therefore has its lock stolen mid-operation, and two writers proceed concurrently: the sync then writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed (the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations).

## Why it was not fixed in SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ
The claim-hold guard now prevents the user-visible damage (a reverted claim), but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Suggested direction
Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative (no age-expiry), keep age-expiry for dead-PID / foreign-host / unparseable locks, and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs. Add a deterministic regression test using the sync-vs-mutation.test.ts git-shim parking technique plus a back-dated lock file.

## Key Files
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts

## Problem
run_tests.py --scope changed maps changed source files to tests via Python/.mjs conventions only (map_changed_to_tests / _is_test_file in skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py). For a vitest/TypeScript repo (ContextHub: tests/cli/**/*.test.ts, tests/unit/**/*.test.ts) a change to src/foo.ts or a new tests/cli/foo.test.ts selects nothing, so the gate silently falls back to the full suite (two npm test invocations, ~10+ minutes plus host slot contention).

## Why it matters
Fast changed-scope feedback is the implement skill's development-time gate; for the canonical wl repo (ContextHub) it degrades to the full suite every time, which also increases test-slot contention across concurrent agents.

## Suggested direction
Extend the convention mapping to TypeScript test files: <stem>.test.ts / <stem>.spec.ts in tests/{cli,unit}/ and any directory, plus a direct import-graph expansion (or a conservative 'same package directory' rule). Keep the existing fallback-to-full behaviour when nothing is selectable.

## Key Files
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (map_changed_to_tests, _is_test_file, TRACKED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS)
- tests/ for the runner's own coverage

# implement.py drive livelocks when phase_parent repeatedly fails to finish a child (no recovery from finishing_failed)

## Headline

`implement.py drive` can loop forever without the epic ever advancing when `phase_parent` repeatedly fails to `finish` the same non-terminal child (its abandoned worktree keeps tripping the `finishing_failed` path); drive must bound finish attempts, reconcile the child's actual state, and recover to a clean startable state instead of re-running the identical failing `finish` on every invocation.

## Problem statement

When a driven child session dies mid-work (timeout, host load), its worktree is left dirty and its item non-terminal. `phase_parent` classifies the dirty worktree as "has changes" and runs `implement.py finish <child>`; `finish` fails (build/tests red on the abandoned WIP) and resets the child status to `open` but leaves the worktree dirty. `phase_drive` then aborts the whole chain with `"Failed to finish child …"` (`finishing_failed`, `sessions_spawned: 0`), and the next drive invocation repeats the identical `finish` failure. Nothing bounds the retries or resets the child, so the epic never advances.

Observed 2026-10-19 driving epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX ("Compile an action video"): 29+ drive runs, each exiting 1 after 600–890 s with `Failed to finish child AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ`, `sessions_spawned: 0`, `parent_advanced: false` (evidence: `/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log`). Terminal children are already handled: `_classify_child` returns `skip-terminal` for `completed`/`done`/`in_review`/deleted and never reaches the worktree/finish path — so the recorded framing "drive must treat terminal children as done" is not the reproducible defect (intake Q1 → re-scoped, producer-confirmed).

## Users

- **Producers / herdr downtime dispatcher** driving epics: needs `drive` to terminate reliably and advance the epic once children are done — not burn 15 minutes per run on the same failing `finish`.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a truthful report that distinguishes "finished", "terminal-reconciled", and "reset for fresh session" instead of a bare `Failed to finish child`.
- **Child owner** whose session was killed: auto-recovery must not silently discard *their* progress without a recorded comment and a clean restart path.

Example user stories:

- *As a producer driving an epic unattended,* I want `implement.py drive` to terminate within one bounded cycle per child, so an abandoned dirty worktree cannot stall the epic for 29 runs.
- *As an epic auditor,* I want `drive --json` to tell me whether a child was finished, reconciled as terminal, or reset for a fresh session, so `parent_advanced: false` always means real work remains.
- *As the owner of a child whose session was killed,* I want a comment recording why my worktree was reset, so my WIP is never discarded silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Bounded finish attempts.** `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` counts failed `finish` executions per child; the same child's failing `finish` is never run unboundedly (limit configurable, defaulting to the existing per-child session cap). Unit-testable with a fake `parent_runner` that always reports `finishing_failed` for one child.
- 2. **Terminal-state reconciliation.** When a child's `finish` has exhausted its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), drive re-fetches the child via `wl show`: if the child is terminal (`completed`/`done` status or `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted), it is recorded as done (`ok`), never reset, and drive continues to the next actionable child.
- 3. **Non-terminal recovery, no livelock.** A non-terminal child whose `finish` failed is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) with a recorded comment naming the failure reason — after which drive continues and the next iteration starts a fresh session for it. `parent_advanced` reflects the true state (false only when non-terminal/blocked work genuinely remains). Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario must terminate with the epic advancing.
- 4. **Truthful report.** Per-child `children_driven` entries / failure reasons distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` (with evidence: child status/stage, failure summary).
- 5. **Terminal children never touched.** A child already in a terminal stage is never `finished`, reset, or re-spawned (regression guard; the existing `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test).
- 6. **Tests pass.** New unit tests cover: bounded-finish-attempts, finish-failure→terminal reconciliation, finish-failure→non-terminal reset+continue, terminal-child regression, and truthful reporting (drive-loop fixtures with injectable `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`). Existing `skill/implement/tests/` drive/parent tests continue to pass.
- 7. **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (and any README/wiki entries describing `drive`'s failure handling) reflect the bounded-recovery behaviour, including the recovery tiers and their audit comments.
- 8. **Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve session-per-child isolation, per-child worktree semantics, and dependency-order driving (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9); the drive recursion guard is retained.
- Never reset, finish, or re-spawn an already-terminal child; reset operations touch only the child's own worktree (never the main checkout) and always leave an audit comment on the child.
- `parent_advanced` must stay `false` while any real non-terminal/blocked child work remains; the parent advances only when every child is terminal.
- The recovery mutation (status `open` + worktree reset) is bounded and explicit — no silent discarding of WIP without the recorded reason.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_parent` (~4978) — the parent-recursion loop; `_run_finish` (~5209) sets `success: false`, `finishing_failed: true`, `next_child` and returns `None` on any finish-subprocess failure; `_classify_child` (~807) already returns `skip-terminal` for terminal children.
  - `phase_drive` (~5620) — breaks the chain on `parent_report["success"] is False` (`~5765`) with no attempt accounting for finish failures and no reconciliation; `attempts` only increments on spawned sessions (`~5546`).
  - `_invoke_implement` (~4903), `_has_worktree_changes` (`~4966`), `_git_path_has_changes` (`~5909`).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status` (`~614`), `require_claimed`/`ensure_claimed` (`~664/707`) — reuse for the reset path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — spawner-command tests only; no drive-loop fixtures covering `finishing_failed` or terminal reconciliation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — documents `drive`'s session/extension mechanics; no recovery/termination semantics section for finish failures.

## Desired change

In `phase_drive` (and minimal support in `phase_parent`'s report), replace the immediate-break-on-`finishing_failed` with a bounded recovery loop per child: (1) count the failing finish; (2) when the bound is hit, re-fetch the child via `wl show` and classify with `_is_terminal_child`; (3) terminal → record as done, continue; non-terminal → comment + reset (status `open` + worktree reset to parent-branch HEAD, gated on worktree isolation checks) and continue so the next loop iteration starts a fresh session. Emit truthful per-child results. Add the discard/reset helper with an explicit audit comment and tests.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (recovery loop), `phase_parent`/`_run_finish` (failure reporting), new worktree-reset helper, `_classify_child` guard reuse.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — new drive-recovery tests (e.g. `test_drive_recovery.py`), fixtures with fake `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — status reset/finalise path for the recovery mutation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document bounded-recovery + truthful reporting.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — reinstall step (post-implementation) because the canonical source is this repo's `skill/` tree.

## Related work

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem statement

`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` never matches a PSI line, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered `n/a` ("unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)") even when `/proc/pressure/*` is present and readable — three of the twelve before-table metrics are dead weight and the pressure analysis in Step 2 can never fire on stall data.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before table to show the kernel's stall percentages so I can tell CPU contention from memory or I/O starvation without guessing."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want the numeric pressure value in the metrics dict so `pressure_analysis.analyze_pressures()` can surface a real pressure with contributors instead of skipping the metric."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want PSI parsing covered by verbatim-content unit tests so a wrong fixture can't mask the bug again."

## Evidence (verified)

Re-verified on this host (16-core Ubuntu, 2026-10-23): all three collectors return `None` while PSI is readable.

```
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=84206005618   # /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=64384303      # /proc/pressure/memory (some)
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=35437059      # /proc/pressure/memory (full)
some avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=398915844     # /proc/pressure/io (some)
full avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=270870893     # /proc/pressure/io (full)
```

Original discovery run (2026-10-21) showed genuine CPU `some` pressure of `avg10=11.58` alongside load 11.92 on 16 cores — real signal was thrown away.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):        # never true — lines start with "some " / "full "
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])    # tokens are avg10=<v> etc., not bare numbers
return None
```

Two independent defects: the prefix test can never match, and the value token needs `split("=")` (not whitespace index 1). The existing unit test passes only because it feeds a fabricated two-line fixture (`some:stuff` followed by `avg10  60.00 60.00 60.00`) that matches the buggy parser rather than real kernel output.

## Desired change

1. `_read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None` parses real PSI output, returning the `avg10` stall percentage of the requested `some`/`full` line; returns `None` when the file is missing/empty/unparsable or the requested line is absent.
2. `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (decided: **`cpu` → `some`; `memory` → `full`; `io` → `full`**) so the semantic choice is explicit in code.
3. Each metric's `description` names the line used and its basis, e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`, so the table is self-documenting; the `n/a` description states which line was requested.
4. `memory_pressure` gets its **own** `config.yaml` block (and `config.py::_DEFAULTS` entry) calibrated for `full`-line semantics — `warning: 5`, `critical: 20` — replacing the current accidental mapping to `memory_usage` 80/95.
5. `SKILL.md` metric table gains a line-selection column and documents the `some` vs `full` semantics, the new `memory_pressure` block, and the no-fallback degradation rule.

## Implementation plan (test-first, single vertical slice)

**Decomposition decision: no child work items.** The change is one Small, self-contained vertical slice (parser → wiring → config → docs → tests) confined to a single skill; splitting it would add coordination overhead without reducing risk. Test-first ordering is expressed as the sequence below and enforced by the build → test → commit gate during implementation.

1. **Failing parser tests first** (`tests/test_metrics.py::TestReadProcPressure`) — delete the fabricated `avg10  60.00 …` fixture, add verbatim kernel samples (cpu `some`-only; memory/io `some` + `full`), asserting the expected `avg10` values and that `which="some"` vs `which="full"` select different lines of the same sample — **AC1**. Verify: new tests fail (RED) against today's `_read_proc_pressure`.
2. **Failure-mode tests** — missing file, present-but-unparsable (`avg10=abc`), requested `full` line absent (documented no-fallback), empty file → `None` — **AC2**.
3. **Parser implementation** (`scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure(key, which="some")`) — select the `some ` / `full ` line, parse `avg10=<v>` with `split("=")`, return `float`, `None` on any failure — **AC1, AC2**. Verify: steps 1–2 tests GREEN.
4. **Config block** (`scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` + `config.yaml`) — add `memory_pressure` (`low: 0`, `warning: 5`, `critical: 20`) calibrated for `full`-line semantics; fix the misleading "Memory Pressure" heading above `memory_usage`; `tests/test_config.py` gains defaults + file-override assertions — **AC5**.
5. **Wiring + description tests** (`collect_metrics`) — `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (`cpu`→`some`, `memory`→`full`, `io`→`full`) and `memory_pressure` resolves to the new config key; descriptions carry line + basis (e.g. `"CPU stall pressure (some avg10, % of time any task stalled)"`) and the `n/a` description names the requested line; a mocked-PSI test asserts rendered values, statuses and descriptions — **AC3, AC6**.
6. **Documentation** (`SKILL.md`) — line-selection column in the metric table, `some` vs `full` semantics, the new `memory_pressure` block, threshold provenance, the no-fallback degradation rule, and why stall % is not comparable to `memory_usage` % — **AC4, AC5, AC8**.
7. **Real-host verification** — run `scripts/evaluate.py` from the worktree on this PSI-enabled host; numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` (no `n/a`); paste the run output into a comment on this item — **AC7**.
8. **Gate** — changed-scope tests via `/skill:test`, and the full suite must pass before any `dev` push — **AC9**.

No phasing boundary is needed: the slice lands as one branch/worktree with a test-first commit series.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 — `/skill:plan` session `herdr-1792903348-145198-13191`: duplicate-work check found no overlapping item (`SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2` is the deliberate threshold-recalibration follow-up — no AC overlap); AC1–AC9 traced to the five "Desired change" requirements; **AC6 extended** to cover requirement 3's clause that the `n/a` description names the requested line; **AC8 made verifiable** against this repository's actual documentation surfaces (no README or docs-site entry exists for this skill); test-first implementation sequence recorded above; decomposition decision: no child work items (single Small vertical slice).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `_read_proc_pressure` parses verbatim `/proc/pressure` content and returns the `avg10` percentage for the requested `some`/`full` line; a unit test feeds real cpu (some only) and memory/io (some + full) samples and asserts the expected values, plus that `which="some"` and `which="full"` select different values from the same two-line sample.
- **AC2** — Unit tests cover failure modes: missing file → `None`; present but unparsable (`avg10=abc`) → `None`; requested `full` line absent → `None` (documented no-fallback behaviour); empty file → `None`.
- **AC3** — `collect_metrics()` wires `cpu`→`some`, `memory`→`full`, `io`→`full` and classifies `memory_pressure` against the new `memory_pressure` config block; a unit test with mocked PSI content asserts the rendered numeric values, their statuses, and that the descriptions name the selected line.
- **AC4** — The `some` vs `full` choice per metric is documented in `SKILL.md` and reflected in each metric's `description`; the previously wrong `test_metrics.py` fixture is replaced with verbatim kernel content.
- **AC5** — `memory_pressure` has its own `config.yaml` block and `config.py::_DEFAULTS` entry (with `test_config.py` coverage asserting the defaults and a file override), and `SKILL.md` explains why stall percentage is not comparable to `memory_usage` percentage.
- **AC6** — Degradation is unchanged: non-Linux or PSI-less kernels still yield `None` and an "unavailable" description that names the requested line (requirement 3) with no crash, covered by a test.
- **AC7** — On this PSI-enabled host, a real `scripts/evaluate.py` run renders numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` values (no `n/a`); the run output is pasted into a comment on this item.
- **AC8** — All related documentation in this repository is updated: `SKILL.md` (metric table, `some`/`full` semantics, `memory_pressure` block, degradation rule) plus code comments/docstrings in `metrics.py` and `config.py`. This skill has no README and no docs-site/wiki entry today, so no other documentation surface needs an update.
- **AC9** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repo/ownership:** the skill is canonical here (`skill/machine-hygiene/`), installed to `~/.pi/agent/skills` by `scripts/install_pi.sh`. Do not patch the installed copy by hand; no new copy in another repo. Note the current global install is a real directory rather than the script's symlink — refreshing it (`scripts/install_pi.sh` or equivalent) is part of verifying AC7, not part of the change.
- **Scope:** parser + line-selection semantics + `memory_pressure` thresholds + tests + docs only.
- **Python style:** existing `unittest` + `importlib`-by-path module loading; no new dependencies.
- **No behaviour change** to action execution, approval gating, or table rendering; `tables.py` already renders numeric/n-a correctly.
- **Stable metric keys:** `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` names must not change (consumed by `pressure_analysis._PRESSURE_METRICS` and the before/after table).

### Out of scope

- Recalibrating `cpu_pressure` (70/85) and `io_pressure` (50/80) thresholds — split out to SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2.
- Process/thread/swap threshold miscalibration (ContextHub WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY) and duplicate proposed-actions (WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ).
- Any change to action execution, approval gating, table layout, or cgroup/systemd resource limiting.

## Existing state

- `scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure(key)` (buggy), `pressure_specs` maps `memory_pressure` → `memory_usage` thresholds.
- `scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` has `cpu_pressure`, `memory_usage`, `io_pressure`; **no** `memory_pressure`.
- `config.yaml` — documents `memory_usage` under a "Memory Pressure (from /proc/pressure/memory)" heading (misleading), no `memory_pressure` block.
- `SKILL.md` — metric table lists the three pressure metrics with "Percentage thresholds"; no `some`/`full` mention.
- `tests/test_metrics.py` — `TestReadProcPressure` uses the fake `avg10 60.00 …` fixture that locks in the bug.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Ubuntu/Worklog hosts run kernel ≥ 4.20, where memory and I/O expose both `some` and `full`. Older PSI backports exposing only `some` will render memory/io `n/a` — accepted and documented (no silent fallback to `some`, which would mix severities).
- **Assumption:** `full`-line `avg10` is the actionable signal for memory/io; `warning: 5` / `critical: 20` are starting thresholds to be tuned from real runs (no data exists today because the parser never worked).
- **Risk — silent green:** if thresholds were left at 80/95, `memory_pressure` would parse but never fire; AC5's own block with PSI-calibrated values avoids re-introducing the loss of signal.
- **Risk — noisy amber:** with `full` semantics + low thresholds, a heavily loaded multi-agent host may show persistent amber memory/io pressure; acceptable (it *is* the honest stall signal) but worth watching during AC7 verification.
- **Risk — masked-by-fixture regression:** the current fixture asserts the buggy format; AC4 must delete it rather than adapt it, or the test suite keeps blessing the wrong shape.
- **Scope-creep risk:** switching `io_pressure` to `full` also makes its existing 50/80 thresholds miscalibrated, and `cpu_pressure`'s 70/85 deserve a sanity pass under `some` semantics. Recorded as the linked follow-up **SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2** rather than widening this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure()` (~line 105) gains the `which` selector and real parsing; `pressure_specs` (~line 352) gains the per-metric line choice; unavailable-description text.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py` — add the `memory_pressure` block to `_DEFAULTS`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — add the `memory_pressure` block with PSI-specific comments; fix the misleading "Memory Pressure" heading over `memory_usage`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — metric table line-selection column, `some`/`full` semantics, threshold provenance, degradation rule.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — replace `TestReadProcPressure` fixtures with verbatim PSI samples; add line-selection, unparsable and missing-line cases; extend the `collect_metrics` pressure assertions.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — defaults + override coverage for `memory_pressure`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVIPKT8L0070OVC** (ContextHub) — source item for this migration; superseded by this item and deleted afterwards.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** (ContextHub, open) — machine-hygiene threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (process/thread/swap); same discovery session, adjacent calibration concern.
- **WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ** (ContextHub, open) — duplicate proposed-actions table/actions; same discovery session, independent defect.
- **SA-0MVLJAG3P0053RJ2** (this repo, open) — recalibrate `cpu_pressure`/`io_pressure` thresholds now that parsing works; deliberately split out of this item's scope.
- **SA-0MUVNZ2QV000LFI9 / SA-0MUVNZ0NU008DTHK / SA-0MUVNZ059002C9Q8** — completed ruff chop items touching `test_metrics.py` / `metrics.py`; no functional overlap, but they explain recent line-number churn.
- **Automated report** — see the "Related work (automated report)" section (retained separately).

## Verification

Changed-scope tests run through the test skill (`/skill:test`), not ad-hoc `pytest`; AC7 additionally needs one real `scripts/evaluate.py` run on a PSI-enabled host.

## Migration note

Migrated from ContextHub `WL-0MVIPKT8L0070OVC` after intake Q1 resolved that the fix belongs in this repo (the only git-tracked copy, and the one `install_pi.sh` publishes globally). The source item is deleted once this item exists, so this item is the single source of truth. Discovery: `discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Where does the fix land (and therefore where is it tracked)?**
  - Options: (A) SorraAgents `skill/machine-hygiene` with a new `SA-` item; (B) new copy at `ContextHub/skill/machine-hygiene`; (C) patch `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene` by hand.

  - Evidence: `diff -r skill/machine-hygiene ~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene` is empty; `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills` → `$SRC_DIR/skill`; precedent for cross-repo tracking: ContextHub `WL-0MQEF8XYR0007BPS` closed against a SorraAgents commit.
- **Q2: `some` vs `full` line per metric?**
  - Options: (A) cpu→`some`, memory/io→`full`, documented; (B) `some` for all three; (C) `full` with fallback to `some` when absent.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — matches kernel semantics (cpu exposes no `full` line) and `full` is what makes memory/io actionable.
  - Evidence: `/proc/pressure/cpu` on this host emits only a `some` line; memory and io emit `some` + `full`.
- **Q3: `memory_pressure` threshold wiring (AC5)?**

## Goal

As a producer, I want `wl sync` to complete in the SorraAgents checkout so locally-authored work items publish, and I want `refs/worklog/data` to stay free of sentinel-authored commits so fresh clones can sync at all.

## Issue

`wl sync` refused to merge inbound worklog data:

```
✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 2 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.
- 893203e8d: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
- dec50d4d6: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
```

The gate is correct (sentinel `t@t.com` must stay refused); the *data on the ref* was the problem.

## Resolution (operator-authorised 2026-10-23: "Yes clear the sync block")

Option (b) from the SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 playbook — re-author the sentinel commits on `refs/worklog/data`, trees untouched, force-push with lease. No `--allow-foreign-author` was used.

1. Backed up the pre-rewrite tip as tag `worklog-tt-reauthor-backup-2026-10-23`.
2. `git filter-branch --env-filter` rewrote every `t@t.com` author/committer to `Sorra the Orc <250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com>` on a temp ref.
   Verified before pushing: `git diff --quiet <old> <new>` → identical trees, commits 2317 → 2317, sentinel authors 2 → 0.
3. Force-pushed with `--force-with-lease` (4 attempts — concurrent agent syncs kept advancing the ref; every attempt re-fetched, re-rewrote and re-verified the tree before pushing).
4. Two recovery deltas published on the rewritten ref to restore records the pre-rewrite remote held but the local store lacked:
   - delta 1: 2 items + 6 comments (`SA-0MT7U2SN9007Z112`, `SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR` + their comments, plus comments on `SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V`, `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL`, `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`);
   - delta 2: the 3 comments whose parent item was absent from delta 1 (added with byte-identical local parent records) — `wl`'s merge drops comments whose parent item is not in the same delta.
5. Plain `wl sync` (no flags) now succeeds and advances `last-synced-ref`; run repeatedly, no refusals.

## Verification

- Remote history author population: `2305 × 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `16 × pi@local` (allow-listed), `0 × t@t.com`.
- Tip tree after rewrite is byte-identical to the pre-rewrite tip tree (`git diff --quiet` empty).
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py --repo-root .` → `OK: git identity is consistent`.
- `syncAllowedAuthors` unchanged: the sentinel quarantine is preserved; `t@t.com` is still refused.
- Data fidelity: all 8 previously-missing records verified present via `wl show` (2 items, 6 comments); no items lost in either direction.
- Fresh-clone gate: whole-history author scan is now clean, so a new clone no longer refuses.

## Recurrence

The two offending commits were pushed 2026-10-23 15:41 and 19:18 from an environment still using the incident sentinel identity — consistent with the RossGameDev checkout identified in SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2. Local checkouts and all worktrees on this host report the correct identity, and every concurrent sync on this host during the remediation authored commits correctly. The push-side guard (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E) is therefore still the durable prevention, and RossGameDev's `user.email` still needs correcting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** The two sentinel-authored inbound worklog commits are re-authored with the project identity and force-pushed with operator approval; tip tree unchanged.
- [x] **AC2** `wl sync` (no flags) completes — pull and push — and local worklog mutations publish (`last-synced-ref` advances past the rewritten tip).
- [x] **AC3** `t@t.com` remains absent from `syncAllowedAuthors`; `scripts/check_git_identity.py` still treats it as a sentinel.
- [x] **AC4** The recurrence source is explained (non-host checkout still on the sentinel identity; concurrent host syncs are clean) and the prevention item SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E remains open.
- [x] **AC5** No worklog data lost: 2 items and 6 comments restored and verified; remote history author population is clean.

# Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN** (implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when child completed).

## Target outcome

A deterministic, injectable test suite in `tests/test_implement_drive.py` that pins the drive-loop behaviour after a child session times out. Written **test-first**: the new tests fail for the right reason until the reconciliation lands in the sibling items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Timeout + terminal child.** A scripted spawner returns `{"success": False, "reason": "Child session for <id> timed out after 3600s."}` while `wl_show(<child>)` reports `status: completed` / `stage: in_review`. The drive report does **not** fail that child, does **not** stop the chain, drives the remaining children, and advances the parent (parent AC1).
- **Timeout + non-terminal child.** `wl_show` reports `open`/`in-progress`. The drive report fails the child (`result: failed`, `failed_child` set), stops the chain, and does not advance the parent — regression guard for existing behaviour (parent AC2).
- **Report evidence distinguishes the two timeout outcomes.** The per-child `children_driven` entry carries the terminal evidence (status/stage, timeout seconds) for the completed-late case and an incomplete verdict for the non-terminal case (parent AC4).
- **Existing tests unchanged.** Every current case in `tests/test_implement_drive.py` continues to pass without modification (parent AC5).
- **Hermetic.** No real `wl` call, no subprocess, no network: `wl_show` and the session spawner are injected/mocked.

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-1: **Timeout-reconciliation pass succeeds when child is terminal.** When a driven child's session times out but the child's work item has reached a terminal state (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`) with its commit pushed to `dev`, the drive report does **not** fail that child and does **not** stop the chain: it records the actual terminal status (result `ok`/`completed-late` with the terminal evidence), continues driving remaining children, and advances the parent when all children are terminal. Unit-testable with a fake spawner that simulates a timeout while `wl show` reports the child as terminal.
- Covers parent AC-2: **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- Covers parent AC-4: **Drive report distinguishes timeout outcomes.** The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
- Covers parent AC-5: **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
## Definition of done

- New tests demonstrably fail before the implementation items land, then pass.
- Changed-scope test gate green through the test skill (`run_tests.py`).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `RecordingSpawner` (or add a `TimeoutSpawner`) to return scripted timeout failures.
- Add a `_patch_child_state(m, states)` helper that routes `wl_show` per child id while still serving the parent fetch.
- Add a `TestTimeoutReconciliation` class with the three cases above, reusing `ScriptedParent` and `_run`.

## Constraints

- Session-per-child isolation and per-child worktree semantics unchanged (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9).
- Tests only — no production-code change in this item.
- Agent test runs go through the test skill only (no ad-hoc `pytest`).

## Risky assumptions

- `wl_show` is the only state source the reconciliation needs (parent assumption A2).
- Per-id `wl_show` mocking does not mask the parent fetch (`wl_show(PARENT)` uses the same function).

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

## Deliverables

- New timeout-reconciliation test class plus helpers in `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.

# Reconcile terminal child after spawn failure

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

## Target outcome

`phase_drive` stops treating a per-child session timeout (or non-zero exit) as a verdict. After a failed spawn it re-fetches the child's state and, when the child is already terminal, records it as completed-late and keeps driving the remaining children.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reconcile on failed spawn.** After a spawn failure (timeout or non-zero exit) `phase_drive` re-fetches the child via `wl_show` and classifies it with `_is_terminal_child` (parent AC1).
- **Terminal child does not fail the chain.** A terminal child (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, or soft-deleted) is recorded as ok, is not re-spawned in that pass, the loop continues with the next child, and the parent is advanced when every child is terminal (parent AC1).
- **Non-terminal child still fails hard.** A non-terminal child keeps the existing behaviour: the report fails the child, sets `failed_child`, stops the chain, and never advances the parent (parent AC2).
- **Reconciliation is scoped to the failure path.** A successful spawn triggers no additional `wl_show` call (parent constraint, risk R1).
- **Fail closed on a bad fetch.** When `wl_show` fails or returns no usable state, the behaviour is the pre-existing hard failure — no crash, no silent success (parent AC2).
- **Tests from the timeout-reconciliation test suite pass** (parent AC5).

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-1: **Timeout-reconciliation pass succeeds when child is terminal.** When a driven child's session times out but the child's work item has reached a terminal state (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`) with its commit pushed to `dev`, the drive report does **not** fail that child and does **not** stop the chain: it records the actual terminal status (result `ok`/`completed-late` with the terminal evidence), continues driving remaining children, and advances the parent when all children are terminal. Unit-testable with a fake spawner that simulates a timeout while `wl show` reports the child as terminal.
- Covers parent AC-2: **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- Covers parent AC-5: **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
## Definition of done

- `phase_drive` reconciles terminal children after a spawn timeout; unit tests from the test-suite item pass; existing drive/parent tests stay green.

## Minimal implementation

- Add helper `_reconcile_spawn_failure(child_id, spawn_result) -> dict` returning `{terminal, status, stage, evidence, reason}` (read-only `wl_show` + `_is_terminal_child`).
- Wire it into `phase_drive` at the `if not spawn_result.get("success")` branch: reconcile, and `continue` the loop when terminal, otherwise keep the existing `break`.
- Do not count a reconciled terminal child against `attempts` / `max_child_sessions`.
- Log the reconciliation at INFO with the terminal evidence.

## Constraints

- Reconciliation is **read-only** against `wl`; no mutation of the child's state in this item.
- Never re-spawn a child already terminal (existing "terminal children are never re-implemented" guard).
- Do not change the timeout mechanism itself (the defect is consequence handling, not the bound).
- Keep session-per-child isolation and per-child worktree semantics unchanged.

## Risky assumptions

- `wl show` reflects terminal state in the main store immediately after the child session finishes. Known store-visibility risk: SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL (open).
- Terminal states are `completed`/`done`/`in_review` status (with `in_review` stage), matching `TERMINAL_STATUSES`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the drive timeout-reconciliation test suite item.

## Deliverables

- Reconciliation helper plus `phase_drive` wiring, with docstrings.

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

Test-first coverage for detecting a child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose work item is still `in-progress` after its session was killed — the WL-0MVGUA9EY003XFAD production case.

- Covers parent AC-2: **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.

# Detect stranded in-progress children

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

## Target outcome

`drive`/`parent` name the stranded child instead of silently leaving it `in-progress` and blocking `wl next`: a child whose session died after pushing work is reported with its pushed-commit evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Stranded check.** A child whose session failed while the item is non-terminal is checked for stranded work using git evidence against `origin/dev` (e.g. `git -C <worktree> log origin/dev --grep <child-id>`, or `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> origin/dev`) (parent AC3).

- **Graceful degradation.** Git unavailable, no remote, or an unreadable worktree degrades to "unknown" without crashing and without false positives (parent AC2, AC3).
- **Tests from the stranded-detection test suite pass** (parent AC5).

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-2: **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- Covers parent AC-3: **Stranded in-progress children are detected and finalised.** A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.

- Stranded detection implemented and reported; tests from the detection test item pass; existing drive/parent tests green.

- Add helper `_detect_stranded_child(child_id, worktree_path, parent_branch) -> dict` returning `{stranded: bool, commit: str, evidence: str, reason: str}`; evidence provider injectable for tests.
- Call it from `phase_drive` on the non-terminal spawn-failure path (after reconciliation fails) and add the result to the report.

# Finalise stranded children safely

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

## Target outcome

A stranded child (work pushed to `dev`, item still `in-progress` after its session was killed) is finalised through the existing `StatusLifecycle` path when the evidence is unambiguous, so it no longer blocks `wl next`; otherwise the detection diagnostic from the previous item stands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Guarded finalisation.** When the child is `in-progress`, its commit is verified on `origin/dev`, and its worktree holds no uncommitted work, `drive` finalises the child to `completed`/`in_review` through the existing `StatusLifecycle` path so it no longer blocks `wl next` (parent AC3).
- **Never unsafe.** Finalisation never runs when evidence is missing, never for a child claimed by another live agent, and never discards uncommitted work (parent AC3, constraint).
- **Recorded.** A worklog comment on the child and on the parent records the evidence (status/stage/commit) and why the item was finalised automatically (parent AC3, AC4).
- **Fallback.** When no safe finalise path is available the behaviour falls back to the read-only diagnostic from the detection item (parent AC3).
- **Tests from the stranded-detection test suite pass**, including the read-only-default case (parent AC5).

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-3: **Stranded in-progress children are detected and finalised.** A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
- Covers parent AC-4: **Drive report distinguishes timeout outcomes.** The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
- Covers parent AC-5: **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
## Definition of done

- Opt-in/evidence-gated finalisation implemented, tests green, and a worklog audit trail written for every automatic finalisation.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `_finalise_stranded_child(child_id, evidence) -> dict` using `StatusLifecycle.update_status(child_id, "completed", stage="in_review")` plus a child comment.
- Gate it behind an explicit drive option (e.g. `--finalise-stranded`) and the evidence checks from `_detect_stranded_child`.
- Call it from `phase_drive` on the stranded path after detection succeeds; record the outcome in the report (`finalised_children`).

## Constraints

- Mutation only via the existing `StatusLifecycle` finalise path (parent constraint: no other `wl` mutation).
- Do not discard, stash, or commit worktree contents.
- Do not re-spawn a session for a finalised child.

## Risky assumptions

- The `StatusLifecycle` write reaches the main worklog store — known open defect SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL ("finish reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show"); if it is unresolved, prefer the diagnostic and record the limitation.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the stranded in-progress detection item.

## Deliverables

- `_finalise_stranded_child`, drive option + wiring, tests, and audit comments.

# Tests: drive recovery test harness + terminal regression

## Goal

Establish injectable drive-loop test fixtures covering `finishing_failed` parent reports and green-now regression tests, so the bounded-recovery behaviour (SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY) can be developed test-first. This is the test/verification slice and must land before the implementation features.

## Problem statement

`tests/test_implement_drive.py` already provides the `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner` fixture pattern for `phase_drive`, but no fixture scripts a `phase_parent` report with `finishing_failed: True` (the livelock entry point), and no test asserts that terminal children are never finished, reset, or re-spawned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC5: 5. **Terminal children never touched.** A child already in a terminal stage is never `finished`, reset, or re-spawned (regression guard; the existing `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test).
- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC6: 6. **Tests pass.** New unit tests cover: bounded-finish-attempts, finish-failure→terminal reconciliation, finish-failure→non-terminal reset+continue, terminal-child regression, and truthful reporting (drive-loop fixtures with injectable `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`). Existing `skill/implement/tests/` drive/parent tests continue to pass.

# Bound repeated failing finish attempts in phase_drive

## Goal

`phase_drive` must never run the same failing `finish` for a child unboundedly. Count failing `finish` executions per child and stop retrying that child once a configurable bound (defaulting to the existing per-child session cap) is reached, reporting the attempt counts.

## Problem statement

Today `phase_drive` breaks immediately whenever `parent_report["success"] is False` — including the `finishing_failed` case — and nothing accounts for finish-failure retries. A failed `finish` leaves the child `open` with a dirty worktree, so the next drive invocation repeats the identical failing `finish` forever (observed 2026-10-19 on AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX: 29+ runs). This feature adds the per-child finish-attempt accounting that the reconciliation/reset features build on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC1: 1. **Bounded finish attempts.** `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` counts failed `finish` executions per child; the same child's failing `finish` is never run unboundedly (limit configurable, defaulting to the existing per-child session cap). Unit-testable with a fake `parent_runner` that always reports `finishing_failed` for one child.
- 1. `phase_drive` distinguishes `finishing_failed` reports from other parent failures instead of treating every `success: False` identically, and counts failing `finish` executions per child (a counter distinct from the session-spawn `attempts`).
- 2. The finish-attempt bound is configurable via a new parameter and defaults to the existing per-child session cap (`max_child_sessions`); the same child's failing `finish` is never executed beyond the bound within one drive invocation.
- 3. A unit test with a fake `parent_runner` that always reports `finishing_failed` for one child asserts the bound is respected (drive terminates; finish attempts never exceed the bound) — AC1 of the parent.
- 4. The drive report carries the per-child finish-attempt counts (e.g. `finish_attempts`) so auditors and downstream recovery can see why the retry stopped.
- 5. A single `finishing_failed` before the bound still aborts the chain exactly as today (no premature reset or reconciliation) — existing behaviour preserved.
- 6. Full test suite green for the changed scope; existing drive/parent tests continue to pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (finish-attempt accounting + new default bound wiring), `phase_parent` / `_run_finish` (report surface; read-only here).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — fixtures from the harness feature; new tests.

## Constraints

- No worktree mutation or status reset in this feature (reconciliation and reset live in the sibling features).
- `parent_advanced` stays `false` while any real non-terminal/blocked child work remains.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC1, AC4 partial).
- Depends on the test-harness feature (fixtures); blocks the reconciliation and reset features.

# Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted

## Goal

When a child's failing `finish` exhausts its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), re-fetch the child via `wl show` and classify it with the existing `_is_terminal_child` check: if terminal, record it as done and continue — never finish, reset, or re-spawn it.

## Problem statement

A finish failure can occur after the child actually reached a terminal state (e.g. push succeeded but a post-push gate step failed). Today drive treats every `finishing_failed` as chain-fatal, so a child that is genuinely `completed`/`in_review`/deleted still stalls the whole epic and blocks parent advancement — even though terminal children are already handled in the classification (`_classify_child` returns `skip-terminal` before the worktree/finish path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC2: 2. **Terminal-state reconciliation.** When a child's `finish` has exhausted its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), drive re-fetches the child via `wl show`: if the child is terminal (`completed`/`done` status or `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted), it is recorded as done (`ok`), never reset, and drive continues to the next actionable child.
- 1. After a child's finish-attempt bound is reached, drive re-fetches the child via `wl show` and applies the existing `_is_terminal_child` classification (`completed`/`done` status, `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted `deletedBy` set) — AC2 of the parent.
- 2. A terminal child is recorded as done in `children_driven` with a distinguishing `terminal-reconciled` outcome (never `failed`), and drive continues to the next actionable child — it is never `finish`ed, reset, or re-spawned.
- 3. The reconciled per-child entry carries evidence (child status/stage, failure summary) — AC4 of the parent.
- 4. Regression coverage: terminal children are never touched by the recovery path; `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test — AC5 of the parent.
- 5. Unit tests with injectable `parent_runner` cover both finish-failure → terminal reconciliation and the terminal-child regression.
- 6. Reconciliation adds no latency on the happy path (re-fetch runs only on the slow finish-failure path).
- 7. Full test suite green for the changed scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` reconciliation branch; reuse `_is_terminal_child` (~786) and `_classify_child` (~807).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new reconciliation + regression tests (fixtures from the harness feature).

## Constraints

- This feature only reads child state and records truthful results; the status/worktree reset mutation belongs to the sibling reset feature.
- Cross-link rather than absorb SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (timeout path reconciliation) — this feature covers only the `finishing_failed` path.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Depends on the bounded-attempts feature; blocks the reset-for-retry feature.

# Reset non-terminal child for clean retry (no livelock)

## Goal

A non-terminal child whose `finish` exhausted its bound is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) — with a recorded audit comment; drive then continues so the next loop iteration starts a fresh session for that child. `parent_advanced` becomes `true` only when every child is terminal.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` failure resets the child status to `open` but leaves the worktree dirty (build/tests red on abandoned WIP). The next `parent` run classifies the dirty worktree as "has changes" and re-runs the identical failing `finish` — the exact unbounded loop that livelocked epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX for 29+ drive runs. Recovery must deterministically break that loop and recover to a clean startable state without silently discarding the child owner's WIP.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC3: 3. **Non-terminal recovery, no livelock.** A non-terminal child whose `finish` failed is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) with a recorded comment naming the failure reason — after which drive continues and the next iteration starts a fresh session for it. `parent_advanced` reflects the true state (false only when non-terminal/blocked work genuinely remains). Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario must terminate with the epic advancing.
- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC4: 4. **Truthful report.** Per-child `children_driven` entries / failure reasons distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` (with evidence: child status/stage, failure summary).
- 1. When a non-terminal child's finish attempts are exhausted, drive performs the explicit recovery mutation: child status → `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path, and the child's own worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`), gated on worktree-isolation checks so the reset only ever touches the child's own worktree, never the main checkout — AC3 of the parent.
- 2. An audit comment is recorded on the child naming the failure reason, the finish-attempt count, and the reset performed — WIP is never discarded silently (AC3, constraints).
- 3. After the reset, drive continues instead of breaking on the exhausted bound: the next loop iteration starts a fresh session for that child (session-attempt accounting continues).
- 4. Reset never runs for terminal children (regression guard from the reconciliation feature remains green).
- 5. Truthful per-child reporting: `children_driven` entries distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` with evidence (child status/stage, failure summary); `parent_advanced` is `false` only while real non-terminal/blocked work remains — AC3/AC4 of the parent.
- 6. Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario (fake runner always `finishing_failed`, non-terminal child, dirty worktree) terminates within the loop bound with the epic advancing — unit-tested (AC3).
- 7. Full test suite green for the changed scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` reset branch; new worktree-reset helper (git worktree mechanics, isolation-gated); reuse `_is_worktree`/`_git_path_has_changes`/`_has_worktree_changes` (read-only).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status` for the status-reset path.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — reset+continue tests with fake runner + in-repo git worktree fixture (ScratchRepo pattern from existing implement tests).

## Constraints

- Reset is explicit, bounded, and always commented; use `git reset --hard <parent-branch>` only inside the child's own worktree; never `git clean` on shared paths (Risk R1 of the parent).
- Recovery mutation is a work-item mutation → runs only while the item is claimed (StatusLifecycle guard), and only touches the child's own worktree.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC3, AC4).
- Depends on bounded-attempts + reconciliation features; feeds the docs feature.
- Do NOT absorb AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 (behind-only worktree mis-detection that feeds the same `has_changes → finish` path) — cross-link only.
